body.statement: The leaves of depth \(r\) accepted by the recursion in \(\text{def:subset-pivot-recursion}\) are exactly \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{LDL}}(\theta)=\mathcal F_{\mathrm{causal}}(\theta)\).  Every reached residual pair \((R_S,(M_{e,S})_{e=1}^{E})\) depends only on \(S\), so the algorithm terminates after visiting at most \(\sum_{k=0}^{r}\binom{d}{k}\) subset states, and the intersection and union of its leaves equal \(\mathcal C(\theta)\) and \(\mathcal P(\theta)\).
body.justification: The theorem turns the characterization into a terminating complete-class algorithm without enumerating DAGs or repeated order prefixes.
body.gap: Jaber et al. and Squires et al. give complete graphical or permutation procedures under different oracle models; the covariance-shift literature has no subset-memoized triangular pivot certificate for the complete labeled fiber.
body.consumer: The algorithm produces compulsory and possible effective targets for small perturbation panels and supplies witness orderings for every reported set.
body.proof_tex:
We first establish the order-independent residual identity.  For a reached subset \(S\), let
\[
 E_S=I_d-Q_{:S}Q_{SS}^{-1}P_S.
\]
Positive preceding reference pivots imply that \(Q_{SS}\) is positive definite: in any reaching order, Gaussian elimination gives a unit-lower factorization of \(Q_{SS}\) with those positive pivots.  Direct multiplication, using \(P_SQ_{:S}=Q_{SS}\), gives
\[
 E_SQ=QE_S^{\mathsf T}
 =Q-Q_{:S}Q_{SS}^{-1}Q_{S:},
 \qquad
 E_SQE_S^{\mathsf T}=E_SQ. \tag{12}
\]
Therefore
\[
 R_S=Q-Q_{:S}Q_{SS}^{-1}Q_{S:},
 \qquad M_{e,S}=E_S\Delta_eE_S^{\mathsf T}. \tag{13}
\]
For completeness, suppose (13) holds and \(j\notin S\) is accepted.  With \(q=(R_S)_{jj}>0\), adjoining \(j\) and applying the scalar block-inverse formula to \(Q_{S\cup\{j\},S\cup\{j\}}\) shows that the right side of (13) becomes
\(R_S-q^{-1}(R_S)_{:j}(R_S)_{j:}=R_S-quu^{\mathsf T}\), where \(u=(R_S)_{:j}/q\).  The same common row operation on \(E_S\Delta_eE_S^{\mathsf T}\), together with the accepted proportionality
\((M_{e,S})_{:j}=m_eu\), gives
\(M_{e,S}-m_euu^{\mathsf T}\).  These are exactly the recursion updates.  Induction from \(S=\varnothing\) proves (13) for every reached subset.  In particular, the residual tuple is a function of \(S\), not of its reaching order.

Now suppose \(t=(t_1,\ldots,t_r)\) certifies \(T\).  By \(\text{lem:range-reconstruction}\), with \(A=W_tL_t\),
\[
 Q=\sum_{k=1}^r d_k a_ka_k^{\mathsf T},
 \qquad
 \Delta_e=\sum_{k=1}^r \ell_{e k}a_ka_k^{\mathsf T}, \tag{14}
\]
where \(a_k\) is column \(k\) of \(A\), \(d_k=(D_t)_{kk}>0\), and \(\ell_{ek}=(\Lambda_{e,t})_{kk}\ge0\).  Since \(P_tA=L_t\),
\[
 (a_k)_{t_i}=0\quad(i<k),\qquad (a_k)_{t_k}=1. \tag{15}
\]
After the first \(k-1\) recursion updates, (14)--(15) imply inductively
\[
 R=\sum_{l=k}^r d_la_la_l^{\mathsf T},\qquad
 M_e=\sum_{l=k}^r \ell_{el}a_la_l^{\mathsf T}. \tag{16}
\]
At label \(t_k\), equations (15)--(16) give
\[
 q=d_k>0,\quad m_e=\ell_{ek}\ge0,\quad
 R_{:t_k}=d_ka_k,\quad (M_e)_{:t_k}=\ell_{ek}a_k,
\]
so \(q(M_e)_{:t_k}=m_eR_{:t_k}\).  Hence every certifying ordering reaches its size-\(r\) subset in the recursion.

Conversely, let \(t=(t_1,\ldots,t_r)\) be an accepted recursion path, and denote its successive values by \(q_k>0\), \(m_{ek}\ge0\), and \(u_k\).  Formula (13) implies
\[
 \operatorname{range}(M_{e,S})\subseteq\operatorname{range}(R_S). \tag{17}
\]
Indeed \(\operatorname{range}(\Delta_e)\subseteq\operatorname{range}(Q)\), while
\(E_SQ=R_S\), so applying \(E_S\) to the two ranges gives (17).  Each positive pivot lowers \(\operatorname{rank}(R_S)\) by one, as is immediate from the block Schur complement in (13).  Since \(\operatorname{rank}(Q)=r\), after \(r\) pivots \(R_T=0\), and then (17) gives \(M_{e,T}=0\).  Telescoping the update equations therefore yields
\[
 Q=\sum_{k=1}^r q_ku_ku_k^{\mathsf T},\qquad
 \Delta_e=\sum_{k=1}^r m_{ek}u_ku_k^{\mathsf T}. \tag{18}
\]
Every residual has zero rows and columns at previously selected labels.  Thus
\((u_k)_{t_i}=0\) for \(i<k\), while \((u_k)_{t_k}=1\).  If \(L=P_t[u_1\ \cdots\ u_r]\), then \(L\) is unit lower triangular, and (18) gives
\[
 Q_{tt}=L\operatorname{diag}(q_1,\ldots,q_r)L^{\mathsf T}\succ0,\qquad
 L^{-1}P_t\Delta_eP_t^{\mathsf T}L^{-\mathsf T}
 =\operatorname{diag}(m_{e1},\ldots,m_{er})\ge0. \tag{19}
\]
Hence \(\operatorname{Cert}(\theta,T,t)\) holds.  The depth-\(r\) leaves are therefore exactly \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{LDL}}(\theta)\), and \(\text{thm:sharp-target-fiber}\) identifies this observable family with \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{causal}}(\theta)\).

By (13), all reaching orders for a subset share one memoized state.  There are at most \(\binom d k\) subsets of size \(k\), so at most \(\sum_{k=0}^r\binom d k\) states are visited, and the recursion terminates after depth \(r\).  Finally, \(\text{def:complete-classification}\) defines \(\mathcal C(\theta)\) and \(\mathcal P(\theta)\) as respectively the intersection and union of this exact leaf family, proving the last assertion.
